---
title: "12. Hierarchical analysis masks"
output: rmarkdown::html_vignette
vignette: >
  %\VignetteIndexEntry{12. Hierarchical analysis masks}
  %\VignetteEngine{knitr::rmarkdown}
  %\VignetteEncoding{UTF-8}
---
Saving or opening a Survey Event starts mask preparation automatically for all
assigned Streams, in sequence. No Stream picker or Create masks button is needed.
`event_masks_server()` queues the saved Streams, obtains current requests from
`store$mask_request()` and looks for matching published editions with `find_masks()`.
The worker verifies matching editions before reuse; otherwise it writes new masks.
Input changes and cancellation stop the worker. There is no processing timeout.

`fluvgeo::write_event_masks()` uses standard terra rasterize (touches=FALSE),
classify (zero to NoData), crop and mask operations. Outputs are compressed Byte
GeoTIFFs with BigTIFF support, using the saved CRS, spacing and shared grid anchor.
No per-cell geometry tests or special edge correction are performed. There are
no application cell-count, row-width or estimated-space admission limits.
Actual I/O failures prevent publication. Sources and saved study inputs are unchanged.

Successful results are published only while their input revisions still match.
The map selector displays already-created outputs; it does not select work to run.
The overview reads saved rasters in their analysis CRS and overlays their saved
boundaries. Reopening verifies and reuses matching published masks. Stale or
corrupt editions are retained while replacements are generated separately.

Trace `R/event_masks.R`, `R/study_store.R`, `R/survey_event_settings.R` and
`tests/testthat/test-event-masks.R`. The backend contract and tests are
`fluvgeo/dev/schemas/event-masks.md` and `test_event_masks.R`.

Reference: [terra rasterization](https://rspatial.github.io/terra/reference/rasterize.html)
and [raster masking](https://rspatial.github.io/terra/reference/mask.html).
